read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Campaigns","content":"# Campaigns

A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer of the brand (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel; it is started or stopped as a whole. Owner: campaign-service; its money: billing-service.

## Money: at least one cap, from the user (owner 2026-10-11)
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what the user has not stated. "No volume cap" or "pas de max" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one, never say one is mandatory. No cards for amounts (`choices`).
- Billing decides if it is FUNDED; its verdict comes back with the caps. If billing holds it (today: no max budget), say it will spend nothing yet; never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. Never judge a mix yourself.
- **Leads only** (a source, then Your Team): we find leads, no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.
1. Know the offer (list_offers → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel (find_sales_funnels → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=).
2. create_funnel_campaign → POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. Ask the caps the user has not stated (max budget and/or max volume); set_funnel_caps with both keys (null = no such cap) → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps.
4. propose_switch_on(action start_funnel_campaign, brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId): refused only while no cap is stated. Show the funnel name, its caps and billing's funding verdict; ask yes or no.
5. confirm_switch_on only after their yes, in their next message, even if they said "just do it". API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"}, only after your user's yes. Refused (no workflow yet, payment): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- list_campaigns(brandId, status?) → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= (results: GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns): THE campaigns with type, status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Up to $1/day", "Not funded"), volume, spent this period, results since start ("still learning" = not final), its path (that IS what it does) and steps. Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign. list_funnel_campaigns is the same read.
- get_funnel_caps(salesFunnelId from list_campaigns, never a campaign id) → GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's raw caps.
- set_funnel_caps: change a cap (starts nothing). Send both keys: the one you keep stays as get_funnel_caps reads it.
- stop_funnel_campaign → PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: stops new first touches now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- Every start is refused while the org's payment is on hold: point to billing. There is no create-and-start.

## Parts of a campaign
A campaign owns one part per step of its funnel, each with its own campaign id and workflow (older per-step campaigns are parts too). Trigger events, stats and runs show PART ids; a campaign-level read may refuse one. get_campaign(part id) → GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId; GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} lists its units (campaignId, pipeId, workflowSlug). To change how a step behaves: `catalogue-plays`.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Campaigns","content":"# Campaigns

A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer of the brand (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel; it is started or stopped as a whole. Owner: campaign-service; its money: billing-service.

## Money: at least one cap, from the user (owner 2026-10-11)
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what the user has not stated. "No volume cap" or "pas de max" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one, never say one is mandatory. No cards for amounts (`choices`).
- Billing decides if it is FUNDED; its verdict comes back with the caps. If billing holds it (today: no max budget), say it will spend nothing yet; never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. Never judge a mix yourself.
- **Leads only** (a source, then Your Team): we find leads, no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.
1. Know the offer (list_offers → GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel (find_sales_funnels → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=).
2. create_funnel_campaign → POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. Ask the caps the user has not stated (max budget and/or max volume); set_funnel_caps with both keys (null = no such cap) → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps.
4. propose_switch_on(action start_funnel_campaign, brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId): refused only while no cap is stated. Show the funnel name, its caps and billing's funding verdict; ask yes or no.
5. confirm_switch_on only after their yes, in their next message, even if they said "just do it". API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"}, only after your user's yes. Refused (no workflow yet, payment): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- list_campaigns(brandId, status?) → GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= (results: GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns): THE campaigns with type, status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Up to $1/day", "Not funded"), volume, spent this period, results since start ("still learning" = not final), its path (that IS what it does) and steps. Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign. list_funnel_campaigns is the same read.
- get_funnel_caps(salesFunnelId from list_campaigns, never a campaign id) → GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's raw caps.
- set_funnel_caps: change a cap (starts nothing). Send both keys: the one you keep stays as get_funnel_caps reads it.
- stop_funnel_campaign → PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: stops new first touches now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- Every start is refused while the org's payment is on hold: point to billing. There is no create-and-start.

## Parts of a campaign
A campaign owns one part per step of its funnel, each with its own campaign id and workflow (older per-step campaigns are parts too). Trigger events, stats and runs show PART ids; a campaign-level read may refuse one. get_campaign(part id) → GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId; GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} lists its units (campaignId, pipeId, workflowSlug). To change how a step behaves: `catalogue-plays`.

Public facts, the same for every person, with or without an account. Answer a question about them at once: no sign-in, no account needed. Same words as the landing (https://distribute.you, Pricing and FAQ).

## What we do
Revenue made easy. We find your buyers, contact them by cold email and book your meetings. We answer interested leads ourselves until the meeting is booked. To start we need only your website: we work out what you sell and who buys it, and show you the plan to confirm.

## How pricing works
- The platform is free. You choose how much goes to your outreach, and we bill what it uses at public catalogue prices: https://distribute.you/catalog
- No subscription, no seat, no setup fee. Pause or cancel anytime.
- You confirm the offer, the audiences and the emails before anything leaves. Your dashboard shows what each reply and meeting cost you.
- Emails go out from mailboxes and domains we own and warm: their own mailbox never touches cold outreach.
- Free trial: there is none, and none is needed, since the platform is free and they pay only for the outreach they choose to run. Say it that way, as good news.
- Fully managed (they never log in): the Custom plan, details from the team on WhatsApp.
- A price per action lives on the catalogue page: give the link, never a figure from memory.

## Their next step
Wanting to start = creating their account. On WhatsApp you do it with them right there (email, then the code from that email). On the web: https://dashboard.distribute.you/sign-up

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.

A source is a STEP of a proactive funnel campaign (it feeds the funnel's first contacts), never a campaign of its own. Rules: campaign-service; origin list: features-service.

## Read
- list_sourcing_origins → GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins: the origins and their feature slugs.
- get_offer_sourcing(brandId, offerId) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=: leads found, cost and return per source.

## Budget and on/off (the funnel campaign's)
- A source spends inside its funnel campaign's caps: change them with set_funnel_caps → PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps (see `campaigns`).
- It runs and stops with its funnel campaign: propose_switch_on (start_funnel_campaign) then confirm_switch_on after the user's yes; stop_funnel_campaign to stop. API: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} or {status: "stop"}. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.

## A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme, linkedin..., I met her at X")
1. add_contact → POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl, email?, phone?, note}: into the brand's own contacts. Needs an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a name with a company. note = how they know the person, in their words (the email writer reads it). One call per person.
2. Confirm in one short message: added; email known, or "we find their email when your campaign reaches them".
3. They are reached by a campaign on the CRM contacts source ("We work the contacts you already have"), separate from new-lead sourcing. list_campaigns (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId=): if none running has it, offer one: find_sales_funnels(offerId, brandId, containsChannels ["sourcing-crm-contacts"]) → GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=, then `campaigns` (created stopped, a cap from them, their yes before the start). Never start it without that yes; never a people list per campaign.
Adding is free. Only if asked: the email lookup and lead checks are paid by that campaign when it reaches the person.

## Articulation
Leads the client brings (emails they wrote, pushed one person at a time) need no source: see `emails-you-wrote`.
"Each time someone reacts to my LinkedIn posts" is a SOURCE (LinkedIn engagement signals), not a trigger: it finds those people as leads; the following legs then reach them.

## 1. Acceptance of Terms

These Terms of Service (the “Terms”) form a binding agreement between you (“you”, “your”, or “Customer”) and BLOOMING GENERATION (“we”, “us”, “our”, or “ distribute.you ”) regarding your access to and use of the distribute.you platform, websites, APIs, dashboards, and related services (collectively, the “Service”).

If you are using the Service on behalf of an organization, you represent that you have authority to bind that organization, and “you” refers to that organization.

## 2. Eligibility and Account

You must be at least 18 years old and capable of entering into a binding contract. You agree to provide accurate, current account information and to keep it up to date.
You are responsible for all activity that occurs under your account, including outreach we send on your behalf. Keep your credentials confidential and notify us immediately at support@distribute.you if you suspect unauthorized use.

## 3. Description of the Service

distribute.you is an acquisition agency delivered as a service, offered two ways: our AI agent, which runs your campaigns for you, and our GTM agency, where our team runs your go-to-market. You provide a website and set caps for each campaign; we find the buyers, write and send the outreach from domains we own, qualify and answer the replies, and report what each outcome cost you. Cold email is the channel we run. When a prospect asks to talk, our AI Instant Call can ring your sales rep and connect the call to the prospect. Any channel we add later is governed by these same Terms.
The Service depends on AI providers, data providers, email infrastructure, and other third parties. See Section 8 (Third-Party Services).
Open source code. The code of our AI agent is published at github.com/distribute-you/gtm-factory under the MIT license. If you run it yourself, that license governs your use of the code, which is provided as is, without warranty, and your vendors bill you directly. These Terms govern the Service we host and run.

## 4. Pricing, Credit, and Payment

Which offer applies to you. The offer that applies to your account is the one in effect when the account was created. Accounts created on or after October 29, 2026 are on the current offer below. Accounts created before that date keep the offer they signed up under, described under “Earlier offers”, and are not re-priced in either direction.
Current offer: the AI agent. The AI agent is free, for up to 5 members per organization. You pay for the work done on your campaigns: each tool behind them (lead data, research, AI writing, email checks, sending, calls) is billed by the unit at our public catalogue price, published at distribute.you/catalog . For these accounts we set each catalogue price at the vendor's list price for that tool, with no markup added. The catalogue price is the one that governs, even where a vendor's own price differs at a given moment (for example a vendor discount, a currency change, or a vendor change we have not yet published). Costs that come with running your account, such as onboarding, chat with our AI agent, and payment processing fees, are billed to your account the same way. There is no setup fee.
Current offer: prepaid, with automatic reload. On the current offer, the Service is prepaid. Before your campaigns start, you pay a first top-up on the checkout page (currently at least $10) and set an automatic reload: a reload threshold (currently at least $5) and a reload amount (currently at least $10 above that threshold). Automatic reload is required for as long as you use the Service. An onboarding advance (currently $5) may be added to your account when it is created: it is an advance on your first payment, and that payment is credited net of it.
Current offer: the GTM agency. When our team runs your go-to-market, the price is the one we agree with you (currently from $1,000 a month plus 10% of the campaign budget, the service fees), and the campaign budget is billed at the catalogue prices above.
Earlier offers. For accounts created before October 29, 2026, the platform is free and each tool is billed by the unit at our public catalogue price, our margin included. Depending on the offer such an account signed up under, it pays with prepaid credit, through a monthly plan, or after use (post-paid), and it may hold a welcome or referral offer, all described below. None of these earlier offers is open to accounts created on or after October 29, 2026.
Prices are dynamic. Catalogue prices are in USD and move with our providers' rates and our own pricing. We may change any catalogue price at any time, without notice, and by using the Service you agree to this. A new price applies to units used after the change, never to units already used. The price that governs a unit is the catalogue price at the moment that unit is used, as shown in your dashboard.
Prepaid credit. You add credit before outreach starts, through our payment processors (Stripe or Revolut). The work on your campaigns draws on that credit. When it runs out, the automatic reload below adds credit; when it cannot (no payment method on file, or a declined charge), sending stops.
Post-paid billing (earlier offers). Where an account signed up under it, you pay after use instead of adding credit first. You save a payment method when you sign up and nothing is charged that day. We charge it for what your campaigns spent when your unpaid usage reaches a threshold (currently $50, then $200, then $500), or at the end of the month, whichever comes first. If a charge is declined, sending stops until it is paid. Post-paid is not available on every payment method (for example some prepaid cards, or cards issued in some countries): we may then ask you to use another card or to switch to prepaid credit. By saving a payment method you authorize these charges without further confirmation.
Card check. When you save a card, we may place a temporary authorization hold on it (for example $50) to check the card. A hold is not a charge. Your bank releases it after a few days, unless your campaigns reach that amount while the hold is active: we then use it toward your payment, only for what you owe, instead of a new charge. We may refuse a card that cannot take the hold.
Reserved follow-ups. When the first email of a sequence goes out, we reserve the cost of its follow-ups on your credit. Each follow-up is billed at its real cost when it is sent, and the reserve is released when it is not. Your dashboard shows billed spend and reserved amounts apart.

## 3. Description of the Service

distribute.you is an acquisition agency delivered as a service, offered two ways: our AI agent, which runs your campaigns for you, and our GTM agency, where our team runs your go-to-market. You provide a website and set caps for each campaign; we find the buyers, write and send the outreach from domains we own, qualify and answer the replies, and report what each outcome cost you. Cold email is the channel we run. When a prospect asks to talk, our AI Instant Call can ring your sales rep and connect the call to the prospect. Any channel we add later is governed by these same Terms.
The Service depends on AI providers, data providers, email infrastructure, and other third parties. See Section 8 (Third-Party Services).

## 4. Pricing, Credit, and Payment

Which offer applies to you. The offer that applies to your account is the one in effect when the account was created. Accounts created on or after October 29, 2026 are on the current offer below. Accounts created before that date keep the offer they signed up under, described under “Earlier offers”, and are not re-priced in either direction.
Current offer: the AI agent. The AI agent is free, for up to 5 members per organization. You pay for the work done on your campaigns: each tool behind them (lead data, research, AI writing, email checks, sending, calls) is billed by the unit at our public catalogue price, published at distribute.you/catalog . For these accounts we set each catalogue price at the vendor's list price for that tool, with no markup added. The catalogue price is the one that governs, even where a vendor's own price differs at a given moment (for example a vendor discount, a currency change, or a vendor change we have not yet published). Costs that come with running your account, such as onboarding, chat with our AI agent, and payment processing fees, are billed to your account the same way. There is no setup fee.
Current offer: prepaid, with automatic reload. On the current offer, the Service is prepaid. Before your campaigns start, you pay a first top-up on the checkout page (currently at least $10) and set an automatic reload: a reload threshold (currently at least $5) and a reload amount (currently at least $10 above that threshold). Automatic reload is required for as long as you use the Service. An onboarding advance (currently $5) may be added to your account when it is created: it is an advance on your first payment, and that payment is credited net of it.
Current offer: the GTM agency. When our team runs your go-to-market, the price is the one we agree with you (currently from $1,000 a month plus 10% of the campaign budget, the service fees), and the campaign budget is billed at the catalogue prices above.
Earlier offers. For accounts created before October 29, 2026, the platform is free and each tool is billed by the unit at our public catalogue price, our margin included. None of these earlier offers is open to accounts created on or after October 29, 2026.

Prepaid credit. You add credit before outreach starts, through our payment processors (Stripe or Revolut). The work on your campaigns draws on that credit. When it runs out, the automatic reload below adds credit; when it cannot (no payment method on file, or a declined charge), sending stops.
Post-paid billing (earlier offers). Where an account signed up under it, you pay after use instead of adding credit first. You save a payment method when you sign up and nothing is charged that day. If a charge is declined, sending stops until it is paid. Post-paid is not available on every payment method (for example some prepaid cards, or cards issued in some countries): we may then ask you to use another card or to switch to prepaid credit. By saving a payment method you authorize these charges without further confirmation.
Card check. When you save a card, we may place a temporary authorization hold on it (for example $50) to check the card. A hold is not a charge. Your bank releases it after a few days, unless your campaigns reach that amount while the hold is active: we then use it toward your payment, only for what you owe, instead of a new charge. We may refuse a card that cannot take the hold.
Reserved follow-ups. When the first email of a sequence goes out, we reserve the cost of its follow-ups on your credit. Each follow-up is billed at its real cost when it is sent, and the reserve is released when it is not. Your dashboard shows billed spend and reserved amounts apart.

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.

**Bliss** (proactive, max 10 $/jour) : c'est celle qui va chercher les prospects et leur écrit. Elle a déjà contacté 204 personnes, envoyé 182 emails pour 63 $ depuis le départ. Le plafond du jour est atteint : 10,06 $ dépensés, les nouveaux premiers contacts repartiront à la prochaine période.
